boundary_rationale: A new first-person divine voice answers the unanswered question that closed the preceding unit, opening "נִדְרַ֨שְׁתִּי֙" (oshb:Isa.65.1, byte tier) (web:Isa.65.1, 'I am inquired of'), rendered “I am inquired of by those who didn't ask. I am found by those who didn't seek me.” (web:Isa.65.1) -- a speaker and scene change from the human communal voice of the preceding lament complex to Yahweh's own first-person self-disclosure, the tier-1 signal that opens this unit. The indictment of ongoing idolatrous practice (graves, secret places, forbidden meat, incense on the hills) continues through its own close, where the attribution "אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.65.7, byte tier) (web:Isa.65.7, 'says Yahweh'; this same verse also carries a ketiv/qere note, disclosed below) stands mid-verse, at tokens 5-6 of 19, before the relative clause naming the incense, and before the reproach and measuring clauses that follow it in the same verse; the disclosure inventory also records a SAMEKH paragraph break at oshb:Isa.65.7, tier-3 corroboration. A fresh koh-amar frame at oshb:Isa.65.8 (“Yahweh says”, web:Isa.65.8) opens a different, contrastive oracle and carries this unit's own close.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 65:1's 'not called by my name', לֹֽא קֹרָ֥א בִשְׁמִֽי (oshb:Isa.65.1, byte tier), as a direct continuation of the petition's 'not called by your name', לֹֽא נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ (oshb:Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19, the split verse's first half, byte tier) -- the two clauses share only the negative particle לֹֽא at byte tier, meeting further only as a root-level tie on two roots, the call root and the name root -- was considered as a reason to merge the two units; it is rejected as a merge driver because 65:1 changes both the speaker (human petitioners to Yahweh himself) and the addressee (Yahweh to the nation), the stronger tier-1 signal, a ground the tier of the echo does not affect.

device_notes: Flagged as a genuine frontier question because 65:1's identity of 'a nation that was not called by my name' (rebellious Israel addressed ironically, per the surrounding indictment) against the covenant-naming denial of web:Isa.63.19 (the split verse's first half) raises an unresolved referent question the row does not decide. The disclosure inventory records ketiv/qere notes at Isa.65.4 and Isa.65.7 (single-witness; no reading adjudicated) and SAMEKH paragraph breaks bracketing this unit at oshb:Isa.64.11 (= web:Isa.64.12, front-seam) and Isa.65.7 (own close) -- tier-3, single-witness, not boundary drivers.

boundary_rationale: A second, formally distinct koh-amar frame opens the unit, "לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה" (oshb:Isa.65.13, byte tier) (web:Isa.65.13, 'therefore, thus says the Lord Yahweh'), a different divine-title form (adonai Yahweh) from the 65:8 frame's bare Yahweh. The oracle runs a fourfold contrast formula opened each time by הִנֵּ֨ה עֲבָדַ֤י (oshb:Isa.65.13, byte tier) -- three further instances, הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י and הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י (oshb:Isa.65.13) and הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י (oshb:Isa.65.14), byte-identical to each other and skeleton-identical to the first (sweep: 4 occurrences over 2 verses) -- “Behold, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry; behold, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. Behold, my servants will rejoice, but you will be disappointed.” (web:Isa.65.13) plus a fourth pairing at 65:14 -- and closes at “because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hidden from my eyes.” (web:Isa.65.16), immediately before the unit ends and a new declaration, “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth” (web:Isa.65.17), opens a different oracle on a different subject (cosmic renewal rather than the servants/apostates contrast).

strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit to include the rest of the chapter's new-creation material as a single servants-and-new-creation oracle was considered, since both share the theme of reversal for the faithful; it is rejected because 65:17's 'For, behold, I create' introduces a new subject (cosmic renewal) and drops the servants/apostates contrast formula, with no tier-1 signal continuing the second-person 'you will be hungry' address beyond this row. This rejection stands despite two cross-seam ties not surfaced by the English rendering: the former-things noun closing this unit, הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.65.16, byte tier), is byte-identical to the same noun opening the next verse, הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier) -- sweep: 2 verses book-wide at that pointed form -- and the next verse itself opens on the subordinating connector כִּֽי (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier); the election token crosses the same seam at skeleton tier (oshb:Isa.65.15 to oshb:Isa.65.22).
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Filed as judgment_oracle because the frame is triggered by 'therefore' (a consequence-clause marker) and its dominant declarative content is retribution on 'you' the addressees, even though 'my servants' blessing is embedded throughout as a contrastive counter-voice -- disclosed here as a one-sentence deviation. The fourfold 'behold, my servants ... but you' contrast formula recurs across 65:13-14 (sweep: 2 verses). The disclosure inventory records a petuchah break immediately before this unit (Isa.65.12) -- tier-3, single-witness, not a boundary driver.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a fresh programmatic declaration introduced by the subordinating connector כִּֽי (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier), "כִּֽי הִנְנִ֥י בוֹרֵ֛א שָׁמַ֥יִם חֲדָשִׁ֖ים וָאָ֣רֶץ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה" (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier) (web:Isa.65.17, 'For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth'), rendered “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things will not be remembered, nor come into mind.” (web:Isa.65.17) -- a subject and register shift away from the retribution contrast of the preceding unit into cosmic renewal and Jerusalem's joy, even though the verse's own former-things noun, הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier), is byte-identical to the noun closing the immediately preceding verse, הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.65.16, byte tier) (sweep: 2 verses book-wide at that pointed form) -- an unmarked front-seam continuity the subject-and-register shift is argued against rather than around. It runs through the peaceable-kingdom vision, closing at “They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain,” says Yahweh.” (web:Isa.65.25), matching "אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Isa.65.25, byte tier) -- the postpositive speech signature, verse-final; the disclosure inventory records a SAMEKH break at this same closing verse, and the unit ends there because oshb:Isa.66.1 opens a new koh-amar frame, "כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.66.1, byte tier) (oshb:Isa.66.1, 'Yahweh says'), on a different subject (the temple and true worship).

strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the peaceable-kingdom vision (65:18-25) from its own opening declaration (65:17) was considered and rejected because 65:18 resumes the same creation participle with no intervening tier-1 signal -- הִנְנִ֥י בוֹרֵ֛א (oshb:Isa.65.17), אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֣י בוֹרֵ֑א and כִּי֩ הִנְנִ֨י בוֹרֵ֧א (oshb:Isa.65.18), skeleton-identical to each other though not byte-identical, the person supplied each time by an attached or independent pronoun rather than by the participle itself -- keeping the whole span one coherent oracle.

boundary_rationale: An imperative summons opens the unit, "שִׁמְעוּ֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.66.5, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.5, 'Hear Yahweh’s word'), rendered “Hear Yahweh’s word, you who tremble at his word” (web:Isa.66.5), addressed to the faithful against their mockers. It moves through a theophany of recompense (66:6) into the sudden, unlabored birth of Zion -- “Before she travailed, she gave birth. Before her pain came, she delivered a son.” (web:Isa.66.7) -- and closes at “Shall I who cause to give birth shut the womb?” says your God.” (web:Isa.66.9), matching "אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ" (oshb:Isa.66.9, byte tier) -- the Elohim variant of the postpositive speech signature, verse-final, its final token carrying no dividing accent; the disclosure inventory records a SAMEKH break at this same closing verse. The unit ends there because 66:10 opens a new imperative summons of its own, “Rejoice with Jerusalem” (web:Isa.66.10).

strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the vindication-of-the-faithful clause (66:5) and the Zion-birth vision (66:6-9) as two separate rows was considered and remains rejected, but not on the ground that no tier-1 signal divides them: oshb:Isa.66.6 opens verse-initially on a herald-voice formula, ק֤וֹל שָׁאוֹן֙ מֵעִ֔יר (oshb:Isa.66.6, byte tier) (sweep: 5 verses book-wide at that verse-initial opener, skeleton tier), and shifts from the second-person address of oshb:Isa.66.5 to third-person report throughout. The rejection instead rests on content: the herald-voice verse reports the very recompense the 66:5 summons announces, and so remains inside the same summons unit rather than opening a fresh oracle.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Filed as salvation_oracle since the unit's culminating imagery (Zion's sudden, painless birth) is a promise/deliverance sign, with the opening vindication-of-mockers judgment content disclosed as an embedded contrast rather than a separate category. The disclosure inventory records SAMEKH breaks bracketing this unit at Isa.66.4 (front-seam) and Isa.66.9 (own close) -- tier-3, single-witness, not boundary drivers.
